title: Operating Systems
standfirst: Processes, threads, memory, filesystems and concurrency — how an OS shares a computer between programs.

description_paragraphs: Operating systems interface between hardware and applications, enabling efficient resource management without direct hardware handling. This introductory course, intended for students with prior knowledge of computer organization, explores these concepts using the xv6 operating system, similar to Linux.
faculty: Prof. Chester Rebeiro, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Introduction to operating systems; OS concepts and structure; System organization fundamentals.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: System booting and xv6 on QEMU; Virtual memory and demand paging; Page translation and page tables.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Memory management in xv6; Process abstraction; Process control blocks; System calls and trap handling.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Process management (fork, exec, exit, wait); Process trees; Kernel-to-user transitions in xv6.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Executable formats (ELF); Exec system call; Program loading and execution in xv6.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Interrupts and exceptions; Hardware and timer interrupts; Context switching.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Storage and file systems; Disk access and scheduling; File system organization and implementation.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: File system internals (xv6); System crashes and recovery; OS security and access control mechanisms.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: System vulnerabilities and attacks; Micro-architectural attacks; Countermeasures; Trusted execution and secure storage.
